chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: 'Do not eat the slaughtered meat of the Nāsibī (or the one who is opposed to the Ahl al-Bayt) unless you hear him invoking the Name of God.'

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: the Nāsibī (one opposed to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for eating meat slaughtered by the Nāsibī according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the status of the Nāsibī (often identified in Shia jurisprudence as those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt) by requiring explicit audible invocation of God’s name for their meat to be permissible. It highlights the Shia emphasis on the slaughterer’s theological orientation and the necessity of verifying the Tasmiyah, distinguishing it from general Ahl al-Sunnah rulings where mere naming is often sufficient without auditory verification.
